explanationMd:
Translate the absolute value into a distance: $|x-3|$ is the distance of $x$ from 3, so the condition says "$x$ is less than 4.5 units from 3".

**Step 1 — remove the absolute value.** $-4.5 < x - 3 < 4.5$, and adding 3 to every part gives $-1.5 < x < 7.5$.

**Step 2 — list the integers inside.** The smallest integer above $-1.5$ is $-1$ and the largest below $7.5$ is $7$. Counting both ends: $7-(-1)+1 = 9$.

**How to check it.** Count by distance from 3. The number 3 itself works; then 4 and 2, 5 and 1, 6 and 0, 7 and −1 all lie at most 4 away from 3, which is less than 4.5, so all count; 8 and −2 are 5 away and fail. That is $1 + 2\times 4 = 9$ integers.

distractorRationale.a: Looks only to the right of 3, counting 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (the integers up to 4.5 above 3), and forgets that an absolute value inequality also allows numbers below 3.
distractorRationale.b: Rounds 4.5 down to 4. With a bound of 4 the integers run only from 0 to 6, which is 7 of them, but the bound here is 4.5, so −1 and 7 are also close enough to 3.
distractorRationale.c: Subtracts the end values of the integers, $7-(-1)=8$, instead of counting them. A run of integers from −1 to 7 includes both ends, so it holds one more than the difference.
distractorRationale.e: Sees an interval of length 9 (from −1.5 to 7.5) and adds one, as when counting fence posts. That rule applies when both ends are counted integers; here both ends are half-integers, so no extra integer appears.

accessibilityText: The question asks how many integers x satisfy the inequality: the absolute value of x minus 3 is less than 4 point 5. The five choices are the whole numbers five, seven, eight, nine and ten.

provenance.notes: Original item. The bound 4.5 is deliberately not an integer so that the interval endpoints are excluded automatically; distractors are a one-sided count, a rounded bound, a fence-post slip in each direction.

independentSolve.workingNotes: -4.5 < x-3 < 4.5 gives -1.5 < x < 7.5, so the integers are -1 to 7: 9 of them. The boundaries are not integers, so the strict inequality is unambiguous. No other count fits. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-math-run13) reached the same answer: -4.5<x-3<4.5 gives -1.5<x<7.5, so the integers are -1 through 7: nine of them. The endpoints are not integers, so there is no strict-versus-non-strict ambiguity. C and E are off-by-one traps.]
